memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: and he spoke his message: "The prophecy of Balaam son of Beor, the prophecy of one whose eye sees clearly, the prophecy of one who hears the words of God, who sees a vision from the Almighty, who falls prostrate, and whose eyes are opened." - Num 24:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Balaam describes himself as one whose eye now sees clearly, who hears God's words and sees a vision from the Almighty. It is a striking claim from a man who, in the previous chapter, was so blind he could not even see the angel his donkey saw. Now his eyes are opened.

There is irony and instruction here. True sight comes not from natural ability or spiritual reputation, but from God opening our eyes. Balaam could only see clearly because the Almighty granted him vision. Left to himself, he was as blind as anyone. Real spiritual understanding is always a gift from above.

He also speaks of falling prostrate, of being humbled before the vision of God. Genuine encounters with the Almighty bring us low. Those who truly see God are not puffed up with pride but bowed down in awe. Clear sight and humble hearts go together.

We should long for God to open our eyes to see Him and His truth. This is precisely what Christ came to do, giving sight to the spiritually blind (John 9:39). Apart from Him we stumble in darkness, but in Him our eyes are opened to behold the glory of God. Pray that the Lord would grant you clear sight and a humble heart.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you recognise that spiritual sight is a gift from God, not your own achievement?
2. Does encountering God humble you or puff you up?
3. Where do you need God to open your eyes today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Almighty God, open my eyes to see You clearly and humble my heart before You. Grant me the sight that comes only through Christ, who gives light to the blind. Amen.
